basis: Rhizomelic skeletal dysplasia and degenerative retinal disease define the syndrome.
Papilloma originates in paranasal sinus respiratory mucosa; anatomical proximity does not establish bone or eye involvement.
Defective airway clearance causes chronic respiratory disease; recurrent middle-ear disease occurs in 4/12 patients (~33%). Situs inversus alone is not cardiovascular damage.
Amyloid damages cerebral vessel walls and causes recurrent brain hemorrhage; both vascular and cerebral injury define the disease.
Precursor T-cell lymphoma. Mediastinal masses do not establish lung invasion; common pleural effusions alone do not establish direct pleural damage.
Spastic paraplegia, demyelinating neuropathy and poikiloderma define the syndrome. Distal amyotrophy reflects denervation rather than primary muscle disease.
The name identifies chorea with amyotrophy and defining red-cell acanthocytosis; no definition or phenotype frequencies support additional organs.
Primary magnesium deficiency is an electrolyte disorder; generalized seizures and intellectual disability define neurological involvement. Renal damage is not established.
Hypertrophic peripheral neuropathy and cataracts are the defining manifestations.
Meningioma originates in the meninges of the sacral spinal cord.
Developmental delay in 7/7; camptodactyly 7/12 and kyphoscoliosis 6/11 support skeletal involvement. Kidney anomalies/hydronephrosis occur in 30-79%; cardiac defects are occasional.
STXBP1 encephalopathy causes seizures, severe developmental impairment and cerebral abnormalities. Hypotonia and spasticity do not establish primary muscle disease.
Inherited LDL cholesterol disorder. Coronary atherosclerosis is a separately diagnosed disease; corneal arcus and xanthomas do not establish functional organ damage.
Mitochondrial metabolic disease with developmental injury; contractures 3/6 and kyphoscoliosis 2/6 support skeletal involvement; strabismus 2/6 supports ocular dysfunction.
Inherited peripheral sensory channelopathy causes episodic neuropathic pain and dysesthesia; no other organ damage is established.
Intellectual disability, brain malformations and obesity define the syndrome. Supplied HPO reports night blindness in 80-99%, although atypical for TRAPPC9 deficiency.
Inherited bile transport/metabolism disorder causes intrahepatic cholestasis and fibrosis; ancestry includes an inborn bilirubin metabolism disorder. No common extrahepatic damage shown.
Peripheral/enteric neuropathy with aganglionic megacolon defines disease. Sensorineural hearing loss and clubfoot each occur in 2/2; ptosis lacks documented visual impairment.
Congenital unilateral destruction or absence of cerebral cortex. Presumed prenatal vascular disruption does not establish a separate persistent vascular disorder.
Seborrheic keratosis is a benign epidermal neoplasm of vulvar skin with acanthosis and hyperkeratosis.
Defining sensorineural hearing loss, salivary gland aldosterone resistance and hyponatremia affect hearing, salivary function and electrolyte balance.
Disease is explicitly located in the pericardium; no additional organ or mechanism applies across the umbrella.
Salivary gland carcinoma and enamel hypoplasia affect gastrointestinal structures; sensorineural hearing loss is defining. Neuroendocrine histology alone does not imply endocrine dysfunction.
Carcinoma originates in the penis, a reproductive organ outside the axes; squamous histology alone does not establish a skin primary.
Epithelial neoplasm originates in or occupies the anal canal.
